newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares extend losses, Telebras dives.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares extend losses, Telebras dives.

text.p: Brazil shares extended losses in morning trade amid allegations that Communications Minister Sergio Motta was involved in a vote-buying scheme to get a re-election bill in Congress approved by deputies, brokers said.
Selling pressure, particularly on benchmark Telebras preferred, led the Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks to fall 2.75 percent to 10,350 points earlier.
Telebras preferred plunged 3.11 percent to 131 reais, and its common plummeted 3.51 percent at 123.50 reais.

Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper today published a report linking Motta to a scandal in which five deputies allegedly took bribes to vote in favor of a constitutional amendment allowing Brazil's president, governors and mayors to run for a second consecutive term.
The bill was approved in the Chamber of Deputies early this year and is currently awaiting a vote in a Senate committee.
The scandal emerged Tuesday when the paper reported the vote-buying scheme in an exclusive front-page story.

Traders said investors are afraid of the implications of the scandal in Congress as it may put on hold key constitutional reforms to be voted by lawmakers and delay the passage of the re-election bill in the Senate.
"It is too early to say, but the scandal may have serious implications," said the head of an equities desk, who asked not to be named.
"At least the reforms may suffer a delay and this is bad news," he added.
Analysts also said they are concerned about the impact of the Folha story on foreign investment in the bolsa.

Other blue chips also traded lower. State oil firm Petrobras was off 1.51 percent at 228.50 reais. Federal power utility Eletrobras dropped 2.69 percent to 507 reais, while CVRD was down 2.48 percent at 23.60 reais.
Market turnover was a moderate 455 million reais ($429.2 million reais).
